account: The National Gastroenterology and Hepatology Program of the Veterans Health Administration ran a pragmatic cluster-randomized quality improvement study of computer-aided polyp detection in the United States. Between October 2022 and February 2023 the program equipped randomly selected VA facilities with the devices; the trial registry names the device as the GI Genius Intelligent Endoscopy Module from Medtronic. Control facilities were given a random deployment date for comparison. The analysis covered 269 endoscopists at 42 equipped facilities, who performed 71,594 colonoscopies before deployment and 35,399 after, and 547 endoscopists at 97 control facilities, who performed 151,792 before and 75,415 after. At the equipped facilities the adenoma detection rate rose from 50.7% to 54.9%, an absolute increase of 4.2 percentage points. At the control facilities it fell from 51.8% to 51.1%. In a regression model, availability of the device was associated with 22% higher odds of adenoma detection. The device did not change the detection of other lesions or the withdrawal time. The authors state that the effect on cancer outcomes and the risk that endoscopists lose skill remain unknown.
